name: Aquila
description: Accessible, ADHD- and dyslexia-friendly design tokens for the BIL/SANd-X ecosystem. Import into any app to keep visual and accessibility behavior consistent.

color._contrastNotes: Ratios computed against WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance formula, not eyeballed. Dark theme: text/bg ~18.9:1, accentText/bg ~13.8:1, textMuted/bg ~9.6:1 -- all exceed AAA (7:1) for normal text. accent (#22D3EE) is reserved for large text/icons/borders (AA graphics threshold, 3:1) since it is calibrated for punch, not body copy.

typography._notes: 'Aquila' is the brand typeface; ship it via self-hosted @font-face when the font file/license is available. Until then, and always as a safety net, fall back to Atkinson Hyperlegible and Lexend -- both independently validated for low-vision and dyslexic readability. Never fall back to a serif or a geometric sans with ambiguous b/d/p/q shapes.

a11yPrinciples: Text-background contrast >= 7:1 (AAA) for all body text, verified by computation, not by eye
Never use pure #000/#FFF; near-black/near-white reduces halation and glare for light-sensitive readers
Body text is always left-aligned, never justified, to keep ragged-right line breaks predictable to track
Line height >= 1.6 (>= 1.8 in dyslexic mode), generous letter/word spacing
Line measure capped near 70ch so lines stay short enough to track without losing place
prefers-reduced-motion: reduce must fully disable non-essential animation/transition, not just shorten it
Focus indicators are a thick, high-contrast color reserved only for focus (never reused elsewhere) and are never removed
No tight repeating high-frequency patterns (fine stripes, moire, busy textures) anywhere in backgrounds or borders -- documented visual-stress trigger for dyslexic and photosensitive users
Content is chunked: short paragraphs, real headings, lists over prose walls -- reduces working-memory load for ADHD readers
Every screen keeps one clear primary action; avoid competing equal-weight CTAs
